questions.q: What is the condition of equilibrium in terms of the rate of opposing processes?
options: The rate of one process is faster than the other.
The rate of one process is slower than the other.
Both opposing processes occur at the same rate.
There is no rate of change in any process.
questions.solution: In equilibrium, both opposing processes occur at the same rate.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What does it mean when ∆G  is equal to 0 for a reaction?
options: The reaction has a high rate.
questions.solution: When ∆G is 0, the  reaction has achieved equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the standard state (c<sub>0</sub>) for a solute when measuring concentrations with respect to it?
questions.solution: The standard state (c<sub>0</sub>) for a solute is 1 molar solution, and all concentrations can be measured with respect to it.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the term used to describe a mixture of reactants and products in the equilibrium state?
questions.solution: A mixture of reactants and products in the equilibrium state is referred to as an equilibrium mixture.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What happens to the rates of forward and reverse reactions at equilibrium?
options: Both the forward and reverse reactions occur at the same rate.
questions.solution: At equilibrium, both the forward and reverse reactions occur at the same rate.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What does maximum yield of products imply in terms of temperature and pressure conditions?
questions.solution: Maximum yield of products is achieved at mild temperature and pressure conditions.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which type of reaction involves reactants and products in different phases?
questions.solution: Heterogeneous reactions involve reactants and products in different phases, which is the opposite of homogeneous reactions discussed in the paragraph.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How do molecules escape the liquid surface during evaporation in a closed container?
options: Molecules with lower kinetic energy escape.
Molecules with higher kinetic energy escape.
There is no escape of molecules.
questions.solution: Molecules with relatively higher kinetic energy escape the liquid surface during evaporation.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the term used for a chemical reaction that can proceed in both the forward and reverse directions?
questions.solution: A chemical reaction that can proceed in both the forward and reverse directions as a reversible reaction.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How is the concentration expressed in mol/m3 calculated from the ideal gas equation when pressure is in pascals (Pa)?
questions.solution: When pressure is in pascals (Pa), the concentration c in mol/m3 is calculated as c = nRT/V, as derived from the ideal gas equation.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What happens to the mass of ice and water when they are not in equilibrium?
questions.solution: When ice and water are not in equilibrium, the mass can fluctuate.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What happens to the equilibrium when an inert gas like argon is added at constant volume to a reaction?
options: The equilibrium shifts in the forward direction.
The equilibrium shifts in the reverse direction.
questions.solution: When an inert gas is added at constant volume, the equilibrium remains undisturbed because it does not change the partial pressures or molar concentrations of the reacting substances.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What determines the concentration of the solute in a saturated solution?
questions.solution: The concentration of the solute in a saturated solution depends on the temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How can a pressure change affect the yield of products in a gaseous reaction?
options: Pressure changes have no effect on gaseous reactions.
Pressure changes can only affect the concentration of solids and liquids.
Pressure changes can affect the yield if the total moles of gaseous reactants and products are different.
Pressure changes can only affect the yield if the reaction is at a low temperature.
questions.solution: Pressure changes can affect the yield of products in a gaseous reaction when the total moles of gaseous reactants and products are different.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What characterizes the dynamic nature of chemical equilibrium?
options: Continuation of forward and reverse reactions
questions.solution: The dynamic nature of chemical equilibrium is characterized by the continuation of forward and reverse reactions.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the context of a reaction with an exceedingly small K, what is the role of a catalyst?
options: A catalyst has no effect on such reactions
A catalyst can increase the rate significantly
A catalyst can decrease the rate significantly
A catalyst can change the equilibrium constant
questions.solution: If a reaction has an exceedingly small K, a catalyst would be of little help.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why does the addition of an inert gas at constant volume not disturb the equilibrium?
options: Because inert gases do not affect equilibrium.
Because inert gases react with the substances involved in the reaction.
Because inert gases change the partial pressures and concentrations of the reactants.
Because inert gases change the temperature of the reaction.
questions.solution: The addition of an inert gas at constant volume does not disturb the equilibrium because inert gases do not affect the equilibrium conditions.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How is the extent of a reaction in equilibrium affected by temperature?
options: Temperature does not affect the extent of the reaction.
Higher temperature favors the formation of reactants.
Higher temperature favors the formation of products.
Temperature only affects the color change during the reaction.
questions.solution: Temperature can affect the extent of a reaction in equilibrium, favoring either the formation of products or reactants, with higher temperature favoring products.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the state of a chemical reaction when the rates of the forward and reverse reactions become equal?
questions.solution: When the rates of the forward and reverse reactions in a chemical reaction become equal, it reaches a state of dynamic equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How does the equilibrium vapor pressure of iodine change with temperature?
questions.solution: The equilibrium vapor pressure of iodine increases with temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the primary factor that determines the classification of reactions based on their extent in equilibrium?
options: The color change during the reaction
The concentrations of reactants and products
questions.solution: Reactions are classified based on the extent to which they proceed in equilibrium, primarily determined by the concentrations of reactants and products.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How does the temperature affect the equilibrium constant for a given reaction?
options: It results in multiple equilibrium constants
questions.solution: Equilibrium constant is temperature dependent having one unique value for a particular reaction represented by a balanced equation at a given temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: According to Le Chatelier's principle, how does a system respond to a change in equilibrium conditions?
options: By ignoring the change and remaining in equilibrium.
By shifting the equilibrium in the direction that exacerbates the change.
By changing in a manner that reduces or counteracts the effect of the change.
By accelerating the rate of the reaction.
questions.solution: Le Chatelier's principle states that a system responds to a change in equilibrium conditions by changing in a manner that reduces or counteracts the effect of the change.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In terms of chemical equilibria, what does "net reaction" refer to?
options: The change in the concentration of products
The sum of all chemical reactions in a system
questions.solution: In the context of chemical equilibria, "net reaction" refers to the progress of the reaction toward completion as it shifts to reach a new equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the composition of the mixture like when a chemical reaction reaches a state of equilibrium?
options: It depends on the color of the reactants.
questions.solution: When a chemical reaction reaches a state of equilibrium, the composition of the mixture remains constant.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How can you relate the equilibrium constant K for a reaction to the equilibrium constant of a related reaction?
options: By multiplying or dividing the equation for the original reaction by a small integer
questions.solution: The equilibrium constant K for a reaction is related to the equilibrium constant of the corresponding reaction, whose equation is obtained by multiplying or dividing the equation for the original reaction by a small integer.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What does "homogeneous solution phase" refer to?
options: A mixture of substances in the same phase
questions.solution: Homogeneous solution phase refers to a mixture of substances where all the components are in the same phase.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What happens at the boundary between ice and water when ice and water are in equilibrium?
options: Molecules from liquid water collide with ice and adhere to it.
Molecules from ice escape into the liquid phase.
questions.solution: At the boundary between ice and water, molecules from liquid water collide with ice and adhere to it.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: When does equilibrium occur in the sublimation of solid iodine?
options: When the vessel is completely empty.
When the intensity of color becomes constant.
When the vapor condenses to form solid iodine.
questions.solution: Equilibrium is attained when the intensity of color becomes constant in the vessel during the sublimation of solid iodine.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: For the equilibrium 2NOCl(g)  ⇌ 2NO(g) + Cl<sub>2</sub>(g), the value of the equilibrium constant, K<sub>c</sub> is 3.75 × 10–6 at 1069 K. What is the value of K<sub>p</sub> for the reaction at this temperature?
questions.solution: We know that, K<sub>p</sub> = K<sub>c</sub> (RT) ∆n ,For the above  reaction, ∆n = (2+1) – 2 = 1K<sub>p</sub> = 3.75 ×10–6 (0.0831 × 1069)K<sub>p</sub> = 0.033.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What characteristic of an inert gas makes it not affect the equilibrium?
options: Inert gases change the partial pressures of the reactants and products.
Inert gases do not change the partial pressures or molar concentrations of the reacting substances.
Inert gases increase the temperature of the reaction.
questions.solution: Inert gases do not affect the equilibrium because they do not change the partial pressures or molar concentrations of the substances involved in the reaction.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What commercial application does the removal of a product have in reactions involving gases or volatile substances?
options: It boosts the forward reaction and increases the concentration of products.
It results in a decrease in the concentration of reactants.
questions.solution: Removal of a product in reactions involving gases or volatile substances boosts the forward reaction and increases the concentration of products, which can have commercial applications.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which law governs the equilibrium between the molecules of a gas and those dissolved in a liquid under pressure?
questions.solution: The equilibrium is governed by Henry's law.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What gives rise to a constant vapor pressure in a closed container during evaporation?
options: The increase in the number of liquid molecules in the vapor phase
The decrease in the number of liquid molecules in the vapor phase
The equilibrium between molecules leaving the liquid and returning to the liquid
The absence of any vapor molecules in the container
questions.solution: A constant vapor pressure is achieved due to an equilibrium in which the number of molecules leaving the liquid equals the number returning to the liquid from the vapor.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: When is the expression for the equilibrium constant applicable?
options: When concentrations have attained a constant value at equilibrium
questions.solution: Expression for equilibrium constant is applicable only when concentrations of the reactants and products have attained a constant value at equilibrium state.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What can be calculated using equilibrium constants?
questions.solution: One of the applications of equilibrium constants is to "calculate equilibrium concentrations."
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: At what stage is the system considered to be in dynamic equilibrium?
options: When the reaction is just initiated
When the concentrations of reactants and products are equal
When the concentrations of reactants and products keep changing
When there is no change in the concentrations of reactants or products
questions.solution: Dynamic equilibrium is the stage when there is no change in the concentrations of either the reactants or products.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the significance of using deuterium in the synthesis of ammonia to demonstrate the dynamic nature of equilibrium?
options: It increases the rate of the reaction.
It changes the color of the reaction mixture.
It indicates that isotopes mix due to continuing forward and reverse reactions.
questions.solution: Using deuterium in the synthesis of ammonia demonstrates that isotopes mix due to the continuing forward and reverse reactions, indicating the dynamic nature of equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In which direction does the equilibrium shift when a gaseous reaction mixture is compressed to one-half of its original volume?
options: The equilibrium shifts in the reverse direction.
The equilibrium shifts in the forward direction.
questions.solution: When a gaseous reaction mixture is compressed to one-half of its original volume, the equilibrium shifts in the forward direction because pressure has doubled.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How does changing the stoichiometric coefficients in a chemical equation affect the equilibrium constant expression?
options: It has no effect on the equilibrium constant expression.
It causes the equilibrium constant to become zero.
It alters the numerical value of the equilibrium constant.
It makes the equilibrium constant undefined.
questions.solution: Changing the stoichiometric coefficients in a chemical equation alters the numerical value of the equilibrium constant.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In a homogeneous system, what is the key characteristic of the phase of reactants and products?
options: They are in the same phase
They are in the gaseous phase
questions.solution: In a homogeneous system, all the reactants and products are in the same phase, as mentioned in the paragraph.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What happens to sugar crystals when a thick sugar syrup solution, made at a higher temperature, is cooled to room temperature?
questions.solution: Sugar crystals separate out when a thick sugar syrup solution is cooled to room temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the purpose of Le Chatelier's principle in predicting the effect of concentration changes on equilibrium?
options: To predict the exact outcome of concentration changes.
To ensure that equilibrium remains unchanged.
To provide a qualitative prediction of the direction in which the equilibrium will shift.
To describe the kinetics of the reaction.
questions.solution: Le Chatelier's principle provides a qualitative prediction of how the equilibrium will shift in response to changes in concentration.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What happens to the solubility of carbon dioxide in water when the temperature is increased?
questions.solution: The amount of carbon dioxide dissolved in water decreases with an increase in temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the primary characteristic feature of ice and water in equilibrium?
questions.solution: In equilibrium, the mass of ice and water remains constant, and the temperature remains constant.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: If concentration c is in mol/L or mol/dm3, and pressure p is in bar, what is the relationship between them?
questions.solution: When concentration c is in mol/L or mol/dm3 and pressure p is in bar, the relationship is given by p = cRT.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why is there no change in the mass of ice and water in this equilibrium scenario?
options: Because the rates of molecule transfer are equal.
questions.solution: There is no change in the mass of ice and water because the rates of transfer of molecules from ice into water and from water into ice are equal.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What effect does raising the temperature have on the equilibrium of an exothermic reaction, such as the production of ammonia?
options: It shifts the equilibrium to the right
It shifts the equilibrium to the left
It has no effect on the equilibrium
questions.solution: The paragraph states that raising the temperature of an exothermic reaction, like the production of ammonia, shifts the equilibrium to the left.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What condition must be met for the existence of a heterogeneous equilibrium?
options: Presence of pure solids or liquids
questions.solution: For the existence of heterogeneous equilibrium pure solids or liquids must also be present.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the ratio of radioactive to non-radioactive molecules in the solution when equilibrium is attained?
questions.solution: In a dynamic equilibrium, the ratio of radioactive to non-radioactive molecules in the solution increases until it attains a constant value.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What dynamic equilibrium exists in a saturated solution?
options: Equilibrium between the solute molecules and gas molecules.
Equilibrium between the solute molecules and solvent molecules.
Equilibrium between the solute molecules in the solid state and in the solution.
Equilibrium between the solute and solvents in a gas state.
questions.solution: The dynamic equilibrium that exists between the solute molecules in the solid state and in the solution in a saturated solution.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What type of equilibrium is reached when only negligible concentrations of reactants are left?
questions.solution: Static equilibrium is reached when only negligible concentrations of reactants are left.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How does a change in temperature affect the composition of an equilibrium mixture?
options: It has no effect on the composition.
It always increases the concentration of products.
It always decreases the concentration of products.
It depends on the sign of ∆H  for the reaction.
questions.solution: The composition of an  equilibrium mixture is affected by a change in temperature, and the direction  of the effect depends on the sign of ∆H for the reaction.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the state of the temperature in the system when ice and water are in equilibrium?
questions.solution: The temperature remains constant when ice and water are in equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How does a catalyst affect the rate of forward and reverse reactions?
options: It increases the rate of both equally
It decreases the rate of both equally
It increases the rate of the forward reaction only
It decreases the rate of the forward reaction only
questions.solution: A catalyst increases the rate of forward and reverse reactions that pass through the same transition state.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is important in optimizing operational conditions in industry and laboratory for favorable equilibrium?
options: Optimizing the color of the reaction mixture
questions.solution: Optimization of the operational conditions, including concentrations of reactants, is essential to ensure equilibrium is favorable in the direction of the desired product.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What will happen to the concentrations of reactants of a reactionwhen Q<sub>c</sub> is less than K<sub>c</sub>?
questions.solution: When Q<sub>c</sub> is not equal to K<sub>c</sub>, the concentrations of reactants will decrease until Q<sub>c</sub> equals K<sub>c</sub>.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What characterizes equilibrium for a physical process in terms of one of its parameters?
questions.solution: When equilibrium is attained for a physical process, one of its parameters remains constant.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the primary role of a catalyst in a chemical reaction?
options: Lowering the activation energy for the forward reaction
questions.solution: A catalyst lowers the activation energy for the forward reaction.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: According to Le Chatelier's principle, what happens when equilibrium is disturbed by the addition of a reactant or product?
options: The reaction shifts in the reverse direction.
The concentration stress of the added substance is relieved by net reaction in the direction that consumes it.
The reaction comes to a complete stop.
The concentration stress of the added substance is relieved by net reaction in the direction that replenishes it.
questions.solution: Le Chatelier's principle predicts that when a reactant or product is added, the equilibrium shifts in the direction that consumes the added substance.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the reason behind the increase in pressure inside the box when water is introduced?
options: Addition of water molecules to the gaseous phase
Removal of water molecules from the gaseous phase
questions.solution: As water evaporates, the pressure inside the box increases due to the addition of water molecules into the gaseous phase.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What causes the rate of evaporation to equal the rate of condensation in a closed container?
options: An equilibrium between escaping and returning molecules
questions.solution: The rate of evaporation equals the rate of condensation due to an equilibrium between molecules leaving the liquid and returning to it.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the relationship between the rates of the opposing processes in dynamic equilibrium?
options: The rate of ice formation is higher.
The rate of water formation is higher.
questions.solution: In dynamic equilibrium, both the opposing processes occur at the same rate.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What type of equilibrium is described by Henry's law?
questions.solution: Henry's law describes the equilibrium between the molecules in the gaseous state and the molecules dissolved in the liquid, which is a form of liquid-vapor equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the standard state for a pure gas when expressing equilibrium constants as dimensionless quantities?
questions.solution: For a pure gas, the standard state is 1 bar.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In terms of K and spontaneity,  what does it mean when ∆Go is negative?
options: The reaction is spontaneous and favors products.
The reaction is spontaneous and favors reactants.
questions.solution: When ∆Go is negative, it implies a spontaneous reaction that favors the products.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What role does temperature play in the extent of a reaction in equilibrium?
options: Temperature does not affect the extent of the reaction.
Higher temperature favors the formation of products.
Higher temperature favors the formation of reactants.
Temperature only affects the color of the reactants.
questions.solution: Temperature is one of the experimental conditions that can affect the extent of a reaction in equilibrium, favoring either the formation of products or reactants.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In what circumstances would a catalyst be of little help in a reaction?
options: When the reaction is very slow.
When the equilibrium constant is small.
When the reactants are in a gaseous state.
questions.solution: If a reaction has an exceedingly small K, a catalyst would be of little help.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: At constant temperature, what is the relationship between the pressure of a gas and its concentration?
questions.solution: At constant temperature,  the pressure of the gas is proportional to its concentration, i.e., p ∝  [gas].
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the term for the pressure exerted by water molecules at a given temperature when they are in equilibrium with the liquid state?
questions.solution: The pressure exerted by water molecules at a given temperature in equilibrium with the liquid state is called the equilibrium vapor pressure of water.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How is the concentration expressed in mol/m3 calculated from the ideal gas equation?
questions.solution: The concentration c in mol/m3 is calculated as n/V.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Can equilibrium be reached from both sides in a reversible reaction?
options: No, it can only be reached from one side.
Yes, it can be reached from either direction.
It depends on the nature of the reactants.
questions.solution: Equilibrium can be reached from both sides in a reversible reaction.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What characterizes equilibrium for a physical process in terms of one of its parameters?
questions.solution: When equilibrium is attained for a physical process, it is characterized by a constant value of one of its parameters at a given temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the state of measurable properties of the system at equilibrium?
questions.solution: All measurable properties of the system remain constant at equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How are the concentration terms represented when calculating the equilibrium constant K<sub>c</sub>?
questions.solution: The value of the equilibrium constant K<sub>c</sub> can be calculated by substituting the concentration terms in mol/L.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the value of R in the ideal gas equation when pressure is in pascals (Pa)?
questions.solution: The value of the gas constant R as 8.314 bar litre/mol K when pressure is in pascals (Pa).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the term used to describe a mixture of reactants and products in the equilibrium state?
questions.solution: A mixture of reactants and products in the equilibrium state is referred to as an equilibrium mixture.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How does the equilibrium vapor pressure of water change with temperature?
questions.solution: The equilibrium vapor pressure of water increases with temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What characterizes the state of chemical equilibrium in terms of the rates of reactions?
options: The forward reaction is faster than the reverse reaction.
The reverse reaction is faster than the forward reaction.
Both the forward and reverse reactions occur at the same rate.
questions.solution: In a state of chemical equilibrium, both the forward and reverse reactions occur at the same rate.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How are reactions classified based on the extent to which they proceed to reach the state of chemical equilibrium?
options: Based on the nature of the reactants
Based on the concentrations of reactants
Based on the color change during the reaction
questions.solution: The reactions can be classified based on the extent to which they proceed to reach the state of chemical equilibrium, which depends on the concentrations of reactants.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the term for the temperature at which the solid and liquid phases of a pure substance are at equilibrium at atmospheric pressure?
questions.solution: The temperature at which the solid and liquid phases are at equilibrium at atmospheric pressure is called the normal melting point or normal freezing point of the substance.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: According to Le Chatelier's principle, what can be ignored when applying pressure changes to a heterogeneous equilibrium?
questions.solution: Applying Le Chatelier’s principle to a heterogeneous equilibrium, the effect of pressure changes on solids and liquids can be ignored because the volume (and concentration) of a solution/liquid is nearly independent of pressure.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What happens when ∆G is  positive for a reaction?
options: The reaction proceeds in the forward direction.
questions.solution: When ∆G is  positive, the reaction is considered non-spontaneous.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What happens to the concentrations of reactants and products in a dynamic equilibrium stage?
questions.solution: In a dynamic equilibrium stage, there is no change in the concentrations of various species in the reaction mixture, indicating that they remain constant.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What does a catalyst do to the activation energy of a chemical reaction?
options: Increases it for the forward reaction and decreases it for the reverse reaction.
Decreases it for the forward reaction and increases it for the reverse reaction.
Increases it for both the forward and reverse reactions.
Decreases it for both the forward and reverse reactions.
questions.solution: A catalyst lowers the activation energy for the forward and reverse reactions by exactly the same amount.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the key role of a catalyst in a chemical reaction?
options: To change the reactants into products
To decrease the activation energy for the reverse reaction
To provide a new low energy pathway for the reaction
questions.solution: The primary role of a catalyst is to make available a new low energy pathway for the conversion of reactants to products, as mentioned in the paragraph.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the practical solution for the slow reaction rate at very low temperatures in ammonia production?
questions.solution: To overcome the slow reaction rate at very low temperatures in ammonia production, a catalyst is used to speed up the reaction while maintaining a low temperature for a high yield of ammonia.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What causes carbon dioxide gas to rapidly fizz out when a soda water bottle is opened?
options: A difference in the solubility of carbon dioxide at different pressures
The addition of sugar to the soda
questions.solution: The rapid fizzing out of carbon dioxide gas in a soda water bottle when opened is due to a difference in the solubility of carbon dioxide at different pressures.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the mixture of reactants and products in the equilibrium state referred to as?
questions.solution: The mixture of reactants and products in the equilibrium state is called an equilibrium mixture.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What type of system is required for equilibrium to occur for the discussed physical processes?
questions.solution: Equilibrium is possible only in a closed system for the discussed physical processes.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How is the spontaneity of a  reaction related to the sign of ∆G?
options: A negative ∆G indicates a  spontaneous reaction.
A positive ∆G indicates a  spontaneous reaction.
A zero ∆G indicates a  spontaneous reaction.
∆G is not related to the spontaneity  of the reaction.
questions.solution: If ∆G is negative,  the reaction is spontaneous.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the term used to describe the point when reactants keep decreasing and products keep increasing for some time during a chemical reaction?
questions.solution: Dynamic equilibrium is the stage when reactants keep decreasing and products keep increasing for some time before reaching equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What information does the numerical value of an equilibrium constant provide about a reaction?
options: The rate at which the reaction occurs
questions.solution: The numerical value of the equilibrium constant for a reaction indicates the extent of the reaction.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the term used to describe equilibrium in a system with more than one phase?
questions.solution: Equilibrium in a system having more than one phase is called heterogeneous equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What are some examples of phase transformation processes mentioned in the paragraph?
questions.solution: The most familiar  examples are phase transformation processes, e.g., solid ⇌liquid;  liquid⇌ gas, and solid ⇌ gas.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What can equilibrium constants help predict about a reaction?
options: The temperature at which it occurs
The direction in which it proceeds
questions.solution: Equilibrium constants can be used to "predict the direction of the reaction."
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How has the dynamic nature of equilibrium been confirmed in the case of sugar?
options: By conducting experiments with radioactive sugar
By using a microscope to observe sugar crystals
By measuring the density of the solution
By testing the taste of the solution
questions.solution: The dynamic nature of equilibrium has been confirmed by conducting experiments with radioactive sugar.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the common term used for the equilibrium condition of a soda water bottle before it is opened?
questions.solution: The soda water bottle is sealed under the pressure of gas when its solubility in water is high, which can be considered a state of supersaturation.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What determines the composition of the equilibrium mixture in a reversible reaction?
options: The phase change in the reaction
questions.solution: The composition of the equilibrium mixture in a reversible reaction is determined by the nature of the reactants.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What does the subscript 'c' indicate in the equilibrium constant expression K<sub>c</sub>?
questions.solution: The subscript 'c' in the equilibrium constant expression Kc indicates that it is expressed in concentrations of mol L-1 (concentration of reactants and products).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is essential to achieve a favorable equilibrium in the direction of the desired product in industry and laboratory settings?
options: Using a high concentration of reactants
questions.solution: The importance of optimizing operational conditions in industry and laboratory settings to ensure favorable equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the relationship between the equilibrium constant for the forward reaction and the equilibrium constant for the reverse reaction?
questions.solution: The equilibrium constant for the reverse reaction is equal to the inverse of the equilibrium constant for the forward reaction.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What does Henry's law relate to in the context of gases and liquids?
options: The boiling point of the liquid
The rate of evaporation of the liquid
The solubility of gases in liquids
questions.solution: Henry's law relates to the solubility of gases in liquids.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: According to Henry's law, what is the relationship between the mass of a gas dissolved in a solvent and the pressure of the gas above the solvent?
options: The mass of the gas is inversely proportional to the pressure.
There is no relationship between them.
The mass of the gas is directly proportional to the pressure.
The mass of the gas decreases with increasing pressure.
questions.solution: Henry's law states that the mass of a gas dissolved in a given mass of a solvent is directly proportional to the pressure of the gas above the solvent.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the nature of the condition of equilibrium in terms of stability?
questions.solution: The condition of equilibrium as dynamic but stable.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What color change is observed when 0.002 M potassium thiocyanate solution is added to 0.2 M iron(III) nitrate solution?
questions.solution: A reddish color appears when potassium thiocyanate is added to iron(III) nitrate solution, which changes from colorless to yellow.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How does a catalyst affect the rate of both forward and reverse reactions?
options: It increases the rate of the forward reaction only.
It increases the rate of the reverse reaction only.
It increases the rate of both forward and reverse reactions.
It decreases the rate of both forward and reverse reactions.
questions.solution: A catalyst increases the rate of forward and reverse reactions that pass through the same transition state.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What happens to a system at equilibrium when the concentration of one or more reacting substances is changed?
options: The system shifts to a new equilibrium.
The system is no longer at equilibrium, and a net reaction occurs.
questions.solution: When the concentration of one or more reacting substances in a system at equilibrium is changed, the system is no longer at equilibrium, and a net reaction takes place.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Who proposed the equilibrium equation known as the law of mass action?
options: Cato Maximillian Guldberg and Peter Waage
questions.solution: The equilibrium equation, known as the law of mass action, was proposed by Cato Maximillian Guldberg and Peter Waage.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What kind of equilibrium exists between the molecules in the gaseous state and those dissolved in the liquid under pressure?
questions.solution: A dynamic equilibrium exists between the molecules in the gaseous state and those dissolved in the liquid under pressure.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What does Le Chatelier's principle state about the composition of the equilibrium mixture when the concentration of reactants or products is changed?
options: The composition changes in a random manner.
The composition changes to minimize the effect of concentration changes.
The composition always shifts towards more reactants.
questions.solution: Le Chatelier's principle states that the composition of the equilibrium mixture changes to minimize the effect of concentration changes.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the significance of the double half arrows in the chemical equation "H<sub>2</sub>O  (l) ⇌ H<sub>2</sub>O (vap)"?
options: They indicate the reaction is very slow
They indicate the reaction is irreversible
They indicate the reaction is in dynamic equilibrium
They indicate the reaction is incomplete
questions.solution: The double half arrows indicate that the processes in both directions are going on simultaneously, which signifies dynamic equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Is the value of the equilibrium constant dependent on the initial concentrations of the reactants and products?
questions.solution: The value of the equilibrium constant is independent of the initial concentrations of the reactants and products.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In what condition does a reaction proceed to near completion?
options: When the concentrations of reactants and products are equal
When only small amounts of products are formed
When most of the reactants remain unchanged at equilibrium
When there is no change in the concentrations of reactants or products
questions.solution: Reactions that proceed nearly to completion have concentrations of reactants and products that are comparable when the system is in equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How can a change in temperature or pressure affect the equilibrium of a system?
options: It has no effect on the equilibrium.
It shifts the equilibrium to the left.
It shifts the equilibrium to the right.
questions.solution: A change in temperature or pressure of the system may alter the equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What does the term "dynamic equilibrium" refer to in the context of chemical reactions?
options: The point when the reaction just starts
The point when reactants are completely consumed
The point when reactant and product concentrations remain constant
The point when reactants and products are rapidly changing
questions.solution: Dynamic equilibrium refers to the stage when the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How does the numerical value of the equilibrium constant depend on the standard state chosen?
options: It remains the same for all standard states
It becomes zero for all standard states
It varies with different standard states
It is not affected by the standard state
questions.solution: The numerical value of the equilibrium constant depends on the standard state chosen, so it can vary with different standard states.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the context of chemical reactions, what does "irreversible" mean?
options: The reaction cannot be detected experimentally
The reaction can only go in one direction
The reaction reaches a dynamic equilibrium
questions.solution: The term "irreversible" means that the reaction can only proceed in one direction and does not reach dynamic equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which type of reaction involves reactants and products in the same phase?
questions.solution: Homogeneous reactions, where all the reactants and products are in the same phase.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What can equilibrium constants be used to predict?
options: The color change in a reaction
The extent of a reaction based on its magnitude
questions.solution: One of the applications of equilibrium constants is to "predict the extent of a reaction on the basis of its magnitude."
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: According to the law of mass action, what was concentration called in the early days of chemistry?
questions.solution: According to the law of mass action, concentration was called "active mass" in the early days of chemistry.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the value of the gas constant R in the equation p = [gas]RT?
questions.solution: The value of the gas constant R as 0.0831 bar litre/mol K.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the equilibrium of camphor, what are the physical states involved?
questions.solution: Camphor (solid) and camphor (vapor) are involved in the equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the outcome of reactions in which only small amounts of products are formed at equilibrium?
options: Most of the reactants remain unchanged.
The concentrations of reactants and products are equal.
questions.solution: In reactions where only small amounts of products are formed, most of the reactants remain unchanged at equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What factors can be exploited to alter the composition of an equilibrium mixture?
questions.solution: Temperature and pressure can be exploited to alter the composition of an equilibrium mixture.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Does the equilibrium constant provide information about the rate at which equilibrium is reached?
options: Yes, it provides information about the rate.
No, it does not provide information about the rate.
It depends on the specific reaction.
questions.solution: An equilibrium constant does not give any information about the rate at which the equilibrium is reached.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How can equilibrium constants Kp and Kc be expressed as dimensionless quantities?
options: By specifying a standard state for reactants and products
By using any units for concentration and pressure
By calculating the exponents of the equilibrium expression
By keeping the exponents of the numerator and denominator different
questions.solution: Equilibrium constants can also be expressed as dimensionless quantities if the standard state of reactants and products is specified.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Under what conditions does the equilibrium quotient change when an inert gas is added?
options: The equilibrium quotient always changes when an inert gas is added.
The equilibrium quotient changes only if the added gas is a reactant or product involved in the reaction.
The equilibrium quotient changes only if the added gas is at a high pressure.
The equilibrium quotient changes only if the added gas is at a low temperature.
questions.solution: The equilibrium quotient changes only if the added gas is a reactant or product involved in the reaction, not when an inert gas is added.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What does the symbol ∆n  represent in the expression for Kp?
options: Number of moles of gaseous products
Number of moles of gaseous reactants
Total number of moles of reactants and products
questions.solution: In the expression for  Kp, ∆n represents the number of moles of gaseous products minus the  number of moles of gaseous reactants.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the relationship between the concentrations of reactants and products in an equilibrium mixture according to the equilibrium equation?
options: Concentrations are related by the equilibrium constant expression.
questions.solution: The equilibrium equation relates the concentrations of reactants and products in an equilibrium mixture through the equilibrium constant expression.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What effect does a catalyst have on the equilibrium of a chemical reaction?
options: It shifts the equilibrium to the left
It shifts the equilibrium to the right
It does not affect the equilibrium
It depends on the specific reaction
questions.solution: A catalyst does not affect the equilibrium composition of a reaction mixture.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How is the extent to which a chemical reaction has proceeded before reaching equilibrium determined?
options: By observing a change in color
By analyzing the composition of the mixture
By changing the pressure and volume
questions.solution: The extent to which a chemical reaction has proceeded before reaching equilibrium is determined by analyzing the composition of the mixture.

questions.q: If you change the stoichiometric coefficients in a chemical equation, how does it affect the equilibrium constant expression?
options: It has no effect on the equilibrium constant expression.
It causes the equilibrium constant to become zero.
It alters the numerical value of the equilibrium constant.
It makes the equilibrium constant undefined.
questions.solution: Changing the stoichiometric coefficients in a chemical equation alters the numerical value of the equilibrium constant.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In what type of system is equilibrium possible for the physical processes?
questions.solution: Equilibrium is possible only in a closed system at a given temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why is carbon dioxide gas rapidly released from a soda water bottle when it is opened?
options: To reach a new equilibrium with the lower pressure of the atmosphere
questions.solution: When a soda water bottle is opened, some of the dissolved carbon dioxide gas escapes to reach a new equilibrium with the lower pressure of the atmosphere.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: At what temperature and pressure are ice and water in equilibrium?
questions.solution: Ice and water are in equilibrium at 273 K and atmospheric pressure.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why is the equilibrium between ice and water described as dynamic?
options: Because there is no activity at the boundary between ice and water.
Because the temperature is constantly changing.
Because both opposing processes occur simultaneously.
Because there is a change in the mass of ice and water.
questions.solution: In dynamic equilibrium, both opposing processes occur simultaneously.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why is a low temperature favorable for a high yield of ammonia in the ammonia production reaction?
options: Low temperature speeds up the reaction.
Low temperature increases the equilibrium concentration of ammonia.
Low temperature slows down the reaction.
questions.solution: Low temperature is favorable for a high yield of ammonia because it slows down the reaction and allows more ammonia to accumulate at equilibrium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What factors can be exploited to alter the composition of an equilibrium mixture?
questions.solution: Temperature and pressure can be exploited to alter the composition of an equilibrium mixture.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What causes the brown color of NO<sub>2</sub> gas to decrease in intensity at low temperatures?
options: The brown color of NO<sub>2</sub> gas is temperature-independent.
The forward reaction at low temperatures results in the formation of N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>, which is colorless.
The reverse reaction at low temperatures consumes NO<sub>2</sub>, causing the color to fade.
The brown color becomes more intense at low temperatures.
questions.solution: At low temperatures, the forward reaction of forming N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> occurs, which is colorless, leading to a decrease in the intensity of the brown color of NO<sub>2</sub> gas.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How does Le Chatelier's principle relate to the disturbance and restoration of equilibrium?
options: It explains how disturbances in equilibrium are permanent.
It predicts that disturbances in equilibrium will not result in any changes.
It predicts that disturbances in equilibrium will be amplified.
It predicts that disturbances in equilibrium will be counteracted by shifts in the equilibrium.
questions.solution: Le Chatelier's principle predicts that disturbances in equilibrium will be counteracted by shifts in the equilibrium to restore it.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the significance of the intense activity at the boundary between ice and water in equilibrium?
options: It indicates dynamic equilibrium with equal rates of molecule transfer.
It signifies a change in pressure.
questions.solution: The intense activity at the boundary between ice and water is a characteristic of dynamic equilibrium with equal rates of molecule transfer.

questions.q: In which of the following plots, an endothermic reaction is correctly represented?
questions.solution:
$K_p$ and $T$ are related as follows :
$K_p=K_c \cdot(R T)^{\Delta z_g}$
where,
$\begin{aligned} & K_p=\text { Equilibrium constant in pressure terms } \\ & K_c=\text { Equilibrium constant in concentration terms. } \\ & \begin{aligned} R & =\text { Gas constant } \\ T & =\text { Temperature } \\ \Delta n_g & =\text { Gaseous moles of products } \\ & \quad-\text { gaseous moles of reactants }\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$
Therefore,
$K_p \propto T \quad$ (for another reaction)
Thus, the plot between $\frac{1}{T}$ and $\ln K_F$ shows a downward straight line slope for $\ln K_p$. Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.q:
For the formation of $\mathrm{NH}_3(g)$ from $\mathrm{H}_2$ and $\mathrm{N}_2$ which one of the following graphs represents the yield of ammonia at equilibrium?

questions.solution:
The formation of $\mathrm{NH}_3(g)$ follows Le-Chatelier's principle.
At equilibrium, $\mathrm{N}_2(g)+3 \mathrm{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NH}_3(g)$ The above reaction proceed in forward direction with increase in pressure resulting in increase in yield of $\mathrm{NH}_3$. But as product $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is in gaseous state and is liquified. So, with decrease in temperature, there will be increase in yield of ammonia.
So, its given $T_1 < T_2$. Therefore, yield of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ will be more at $T_1$ than $T_2$.
The graph in option (a) represents correct yield of $\mathrm{NH}_3$.

questions.q:
Decomposition of \(\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4(\mathrm{~g})\) takes place as follows: \(\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{~g})\) ' \(D\) ' is the vapour density at initial stage and ' \(d\) ' is the vapour density at equilibrium. We get following graph when the degree of dissociation ' \(\alpha\) ' is plotted against ( \(D / d\) )
What is the value of \(\frac{\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{d}}\) at A ?
questions.solution:
For \(\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4 \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO}_2\), the relation is
\(\frac{D}{d}=1+\alpha\)
At point A, \(\alpha=0\), so
\(\frac{D}{d}=1\)

questions.q:
The equilibrium constant for the following reaction
\(\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g}) \text { is } \mathrm{K}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]^2}{\mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4}\)
Which of the following graph is correct?
questions.solution:
Reaction:
\(\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{~g}), \quad \mathrm{K}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]^2}{\left[\mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right]}\)
From equilibrium expression:
\(\left[\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right]=\frac{\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]^2}{\mathrm{~K}}\)
Thus, \(\left[\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right] \propto\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]^2\).
So the correct graph is \(\left[\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right]\) vs \(\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]\) is parabola (upward curve).
That matches option (c).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: For the dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl}_{5(\mathrm{~g})}\), the variation of \((1+\alpha)\) against \(\left(\frac{\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{d}}\right)\) is represented as.
questions.solution:
\(\text { Let the degree of dissociation }=\alpha \text {. }\)
- Initial moles = 1
- At equilibrium:
- \(P C l_5=1-\alpha\)
- \(\mathrm{PCl}_3=\alpha\)
- \(C l_2=\alpha\)
So, total moles \(=1+\alpha\).
Average molar mass:
\(M=\frac{M_{P C l_5}}{1+\alpha}\)
Vapour density at equilibrium:
\(d=\frac{M}{2}=\frac{D}{1+\alpha}, \quad \text { where } D=\frac{M_{P C l_5}}{2}\)
Thus:
\(\frac{D}{d}=1+\alpha\)
Hence, ( \(1+\alpha\) ) vs \(\frac{D}{d}\) is a straight line through origin.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: For the chemical equilibrium \(\mathrm{CaCO}_3(\mathrm{~s}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CaO}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ}\) can be determined from which one of the following graphs?
questions.solution:
Reaction:
\(\mathrm{CaCO}_3(s) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CaO}(s)+\mathrm{CO}_2(g)\)
Equilibrium constant:
\(K_p=P_{C O_2}\)
From van't Hoff equation:
\(\ln K=-\frac{\Delta H^{\circ}}{R} \cdot \frac{1}{T}+C\)
So,
\(\ln P_{\mathrm{CO}_2} \text { vs } \frac{1}{T} \text { is a straight line with slope }-\frac{\Delta H^{\circ}}{R}\)
Or equivalently,
\(\log P_{\mathrm{CO}_2} \text { vs } \frac{1}{T}\)
must be a straight line with negative slope.

questions.q:

questions.q:
Assertion : Increasing the concentration of \(\mathrm{H}_2\) will increase magnitude of equilibrium constant of the reaction

Reason : Value of \(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{C}}\) depends upon the concentration of reactants and products taken.

questions.q:
Assertion : For equilibrium Ice \(\rightleftharpoons\) Water on increasing temperature and pressure more of water will form.
Reason : Forward reaction is endothermic and volume decreases on product side.
options: If both Assertion & Reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion, then mark (1).
If both Assertion & Reason are true but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion, then mark (2).
If Assertion is true statement but Reason is false, then mark (3).
If both Assertion and Reason are false statements, then mark (4).
questions.solution:
Heat + ice \(\rightleftharpoons\) water
On increasing pressure, volume decreases. For water, decrease in volume of water is less (\(\because\) density increase)

questions.q:
Assertion : A catalyst does not alter the equilibrium constant of a reaction.
Reason : A catalyst does not alter the position of chemical equilibrium.
options: If both Assertion & Reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion, then mark (1).

If Assertion is true statement but Reason is false, then mark (3).
If both Assertion and Reason are false statements, then mark (4).
questions.solution: A catalyst neither alters position of chemical equilibrium, nor does it alter the equilibrium constant. It just facilitates the reaction.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q:
Given below are two statements; one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R) .
Assertion (A) : For any chemical reaction at a particular temperature the equilibrium constant is fixed and is a characteristic property.
Reason (R) : Equilibrium constant is independent of temperature.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
- Assertion (A): For any chemical reaction at a particular temperature the equilibrium constant is fixed and is a characteristic property.
Correct. At a given temperature, \(K\) is constant and unique for the reaction.
- Reason (R): Equilibrium constant is independent of temperature.
Wrong. Actually, \(K\) depends on temperature (Van't Hoff equation shows this).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q:
Given below are two statements; one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R).
Assertion (A) : In the dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) at constant pressure and temperature addition of helium at equilibrium increases the dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\).
Reason (R) : Equilibrium constant changes only with change in temperature.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
- Assertion (A): In the dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) at constant pressure and temperature, addition of helium at equilibrium increases the dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\).
Correct.
Reaction:
\(\mathrm{PCl}_5(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_3(g)+\mathrm{Cl}_2(g)\)
Number of moles increases (\(1 \rightarrow 2\)).
- If He is added at constant volume, no effect on equilibrium (only partial pressures change proportionally).
- If He is added at constant pressure, the system volume increases. Partial pressures of reactants and products decrease, shifting equilibrium towards more gaseous moles \(\rightarrow\) increased dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\).
- Reason (R): Equilibrium constant changes only with change in temperature.
Correct. This is a fundamental property of equilibrium constants.
But \(X(\mathrm{R})\) is not the correct explanation of \((\mathrm{A})\).
The shift of equilibrium with helium addition is explained by Le Chatelier's Principle and change in partial pressures, not by equilibrium constant.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q:
Given below are two statements; one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R).
Assertion (A) : Solubility of a gas in water decreases with increase in temperature.
Reason (R) : Dissolution of a gas in water is an exothermic process.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
- Assertion (A): Solubility of a gas in water decreases with increase in temperature.
Correct.
Most gases dissolve in water exothermically. According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature shifts equilibrium in the opposite direction (less dissolution), hence solubility decreases.
- Reason (R): Dissolution of a gas in water is an exothermic process.
Correct.
Heat is released when gas molecules are captured by water molecules (due to intermolecular attractions).
Here, (R) correctly explains (A) \(\rightarrow\) higher temperature adds heat, so equilibrium shifts to gas phase, reducing solubility.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q:
At high temperature, the following reaction occurs
4CuOs⇌2Cu2Os+O2g
Consider the following statements regarding reaction
1. Kp=pO2
2. Kp depends upon the amounts of CuO and Cu2O
3. Kp<<Kc
4. Kp>Kc
Of the statements
questions.solution:
Kp=pO2 is correct.
O2g∝pO2
Kp=Kc(RT)Δng
Δng= Number of mol gaseous (Products – Reactants)
Here Δng=1
So Kp>Kc

questions.q:
For a reaction As⇌Bs+Cg the set of all correct statements are

a) K is independent of A.

b) K is dependent on partial pressure of C at a given temperature.

c) ΔH will be independent of temperature.

d) ΔH is independent of the catalyst addition.
questions.solution:
Given reaction is 

As⇌Bs+Cg

Equilibrium constant for this reaction KC = C concentration of solid is considered as one during heterogenous equilibrium. So, as we can see K is independent of A.

Similarly KP = PC So, K is dependent on partial pressure of C.

Note: Although the value of equilibrium constant does not depend on concentration of reactants or products at a given temperature.

Enthalpy change depends on temperature, but it is independent of catalyst used.

So, statement a,b and d are correct.

Match the following pKa values.
$\begin{array}{|l|l|} \hline & \text{Acid} & & \text{pKa} \\ \hline \text{(a)} & \text{Phenol} & \text{(i)} & 16 \\ \hline \text{(b)} & \text{p-Nitrophenol} & \text{(ii)} & 0.78 \\ \hline \text{(c)} & \text{Ethanol} & \text{(iii)} & 10 \\ \hline \text{(d)} & \text{Picric acid} & \text{(iv)} & 7.1 \\ \hline \end{array}
questions.solution:
The compound will be more acidic when its conjugate base is more stable. In case of these given compounds, more the
electron with the drawing group, present more the compound will be more acidic.

questions.q:
Match the column I with column II and mark the appropriate choice.

Column I Column II
(p) Liquid ⇌ vapour (i) Saturated solution
(q) Solid ⇌ liquid (ii) Boiling point
(r) Solid ⇌ vapour (iii) Sublimation point
(s) Solute(s) ⇌ solute (solution) (iv) Melting point
questions.solution:
(p) Liquid ⇌ vapour equilibrium exists at the boiling point

(q) Solid ⇌ liquid equilibrium exists at the melting point

(r) Solid ⇌ vapour equilibrium exists at the sublimation point

(s) Solute (s) ⇌ Solute (solution) equilibrium exists in a saturated solution.
